newsitem.title: USA: Gelman Sciences merger plans hurt Q4 sales.
newsitem.headline: Gelman Sciences merger plans hurt Q4 sales.

text.p: Gelman Sciences Inc said Thursday its planned merger with Memtec Ltd hurt sales in the fourth quarter ended July 31, but some of the lost sales were recovered in August.

"The company believes a portion of the lost fourth quarter sales, caused by the Memtec announcement, were recovered in August as sales were up 27 percent versus August 1995," Gelman Sciences said in a statement.
Gelman reported fourth quarter sales of $28.1 million versus $28.4 million last year. The company reported a net loss of $0.25 a share compared with earnings of $0.27 in 1995.
The company said its plans to merge with Memtec, an Australia-based materials sciences purification and separtation business, caused uncertainty among its employees, distributors and customers.
Gelman said the merger should boost growth by expanding the company's product lines and geographic coverage.

In addition, sales credits for the quarter reached $2.8 million, up from $1.5 million in 1995, as a result of changes in Gelman's credit policy, sales tracking and one-time product returns in exchange for long-term purchase commitments.

The company said it increased its reserve for environmental remediation by $2.8 million after reviewing operating expenses for the revised plan to clean up the ground water at Gelman's Ann Arbor plant.
Gelman reported $1 million in inventory costing adjustments, also adding to the fourth quarter loss.

"The increase in the amount of sales credits, the addition to the reserve for environmental remediation and the inventory adjustments negatively impacted fourth quarter after-tax earnings by $3.4 million or $0.41 a share," Gelman said.
